rules.name: Model Risk Management — PRA SS1/23 Compliance
rules.source_legislation: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 — Model Risk Management Principles for Banks
rules.description: The bank must maintain a comprehensive model risk management (MRM) framework covering a complete model inventory, tiering of models by materiality and complexity, independent model validation, a defined model risk appetite, Senior Manager accountability for model risk, and periodic review of model performance. Models used for regulatory capital, credit decisioning, IFRS 9 provisioning, stress testing, and fraud detection are all in scope. AI/ML models are explicitly covered and require additional explainability and bias testing.
approval_chain: Senior Manager (Risk Management — SMF7 or equivalent)
disclosure_obligations: Annual model risk report to the Board Risk Committee
Model inventory and validation status shared with PRA on supervisory request
Pillar 2A model risk add-on methodology disclosed in ICAAP
AI/ML model governance documentation available for PRA review under DP5/22 expectations
constraints: All material models must be independently validated before production deployment and annually thereafter
Model validators must be organisationally independent from model developers
Models in use must have an assigned model owner with documented accountability
Model risk appetite (expressed as maximum tolerable model error impact on capital) must be set and monitored
AI/ML models must include bias testing results, explainability assessments, and distribution shift monitoring

rules.name: Operational Resilience — Impact Tolerances for Important Business Services
rules.source_legislation: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/21 — Operational Resilience; FCA PS21/3; Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 Part 5
rules.description: The bank must identify its important business services (IBS), set board-approved impact tolerances for each, and demonstrate through severe-but-plausible scenario testing that it can remain within those tolerances. From March 2025, PRA supervision focuses on evidence of remediation of vulnerabilities identified in self-assessments, quality of scenario testing, and board-level ownership. IBS for Risk Management include credit risk decisioning, fraud monitoring, and market risk reporting systems.
disclosure_obligations: Annual operational resilience self-assessment submitted to PRA
Board-approved impact tolerance schedule on file and reviewed annually
Material operational incidents reported to PRA within 4 hours (initial notification) and 24 hours (full report)
Consumer-facing communication issued within prescribed timeframe if customer-impacting IBS breach occurs
constraints: Impact tolerances must be set in terms of time (maximum tolerable disruption) and customer harm
Severe-but-plausible scenario tests must be run annually and after material system changes
Remediation plans for identified vulnerabilities must be reviewed by the Board Risk Committee
Cannot outsource accountability for IBS continuity — Senior Manager must retain responsibility

rules.name: Basel 3.1 FRTB — Market Risk Capital under Standardised Approach
rules.source_legislation: PRA PS17/23 (UK Basel 3.1 transposition); CRR2; Fundamental Review of the Trading Book (FRTB) standards
rules.description: The Fundamental Review of the Trading Book (FRTB) Standardised Approach (Sensitivity-Based Approach, SBA) is mandatory for market risk capital calculation from 1 January 2026 (UK implementation date). Legacy VaR-based market risk measurement must be replaced or supplemented with sensitivities infrastructure. Desk-level approval (trading desk boundary and boundary conditions) must be documented. P&L Attribution Testing required for any bank seeking Internal Models Approach approval.
disclosure_obligations: COREP market risk returns migrated to FRTB SBA format from 1 January 2026
Trading desk boundary conditions and desk-level capital documentation filed with PRA
Pillar 3 FRTB SBA disclosures in annual and interim reports from 2026
constraints: FRTB SBA mandatory for all in-scope trading book positions from 1 January 2026
Internal Models Approach (IMA) requires PRA pre-approval — very few banks expected to qualify
Trading book / banking book boundary must be documented and any reclassification approved by Risk Management
Sensitivity data for SBA must be produced at trade-level granularity — aggregate proxies not acceptable

rules.name: Climate Risk Integration into Credit Models — PRA Supervisory Expectations
rules.source_legislation: PRA Supervisory Statement SS3/19 (Climate-related financial risks); PRA Dear CEO letter (2022–2023 climate expectations); NGFS scenarios
rules.description: The bank must integrate physical and transition climate risk into its credit risk models, ICAAP stress testing, and loan impairment assessment. PRA expects banks to assess the climate risk exposure of their commercial real estate and corporate lending books using NGFS climate scenarios. Material climate risk exposures must be disclosed under TCFD-aligned reporting. Risk appetite for climate-related credit risk must be set and monitored.
disclosure_obligations: TCFD-aligned climate risk disclosures in Annual Report (mandatory for large banks)
Climate scenario analysis results included in ICAAP and Pillar 3 supplementary disclosures
PRA Climate Capital Guidance compliance status reported in supervisory dialogue
constraints: Climate risk must be integrated into credit risk appetite statements and sector-level limits
NGFS orderly transition, disorderly transition, and hot-house world scenarios must all be modelled
Physical and transition risk exposure data must be available at loan-level for the commercial real estate and large corporate portfolios

rules.name: AI Act Compliance for High-Risk AI Systems
rules.source_legislation: EU AI Act (applicable to UK firms with EU operations or EU-facing AI systems); FCA/Bank of England DP5/22 — AI and Machine Learning
rules.description: The EU AI Act classifies credit scoring, AML transaction monitoring, and fraud detection models as high-risk AI systems. UK firms with EU operations or deploying AI to EU customers must meet AI Act requirements: human oversight, transparency and explainability, robustness testing, bias monitoring, and registration in the EU AI database. The UK FCA/BoE DP5/22 expectations on ML model governance closely align with AI Act requirements, creating a de facto convergence.
disclosure_obligations: High-risk AI system registration in EU AI database for systems deployed to EU customers
Transparency notice to customers when AI/ML is used in credit decisioning
Annual AI model risk review report to the Board
Bias testing results documented and available for regulatory inspection
constraints: High-risk AI systems must have human oversight mechanisms — fully autonomous credit decisions above a materiality threshold are prohibited
Training data used for credit scoring and AML models must be documented for bias and representativeness
Explainability must be sufficient to support customer appeals against automated credit decisions

rules.name: FRTB Internal Models Approach — PRA Approval Process
rules.source_legislation: PRA PS17/23 FRTB Internal Models Approach (IMA); EBA IMA guidelines (onshored)
rules.description: Banks that wish to use the FRTB Internal Models Approach for market risk capital must obtain PRA pre-approval at the trading desk level. Approval requires P&L Attribution Testing (PLAT), back-testing, Expected Shortfall model validation, and desk-level boundary conditions. Given the stringency of PRA requirements, most mid-tier UK banks are expected to use the FRTB Standardised Approach. If the bank seeks IMA approval for any desk, a structured regulatory approval programme must be initiated.
disclosure_obligations: PRA application for IMA approval submitted with full model documentation and back-test results
Ongoing P&L Attribution Test results reported to PRA quarterly post-approval
IMA desk boundary changes notified to PRA before implementation
constraints: IMA approval is required per trading desk — not firm-wide; denied desks must use FRTB SA
P&L Attribution Test failure triggers automatic fallback to FRTB SA for the affected desk
IMA models require independent validation annually and after material model changes
